memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The sons of Japheth... The maritime peoples spread out into their territories by their clans within their nations, each with its own language. - Gen 10:2-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here begins the great spreading-out of humanity. From Japheth's line came peoples who scattered across coastlands and territories, "each with its own language," each within their nations. Rather than getting lost in the unfamiliar names, lift your eyes to the big picture: God is the God of all these peoples. Every nation, every language, every distant coastland traces back to Him.

This is a truth we must not miss. God is not the God of one tribe or one nation only. From the very beginning, His purposes embraced the whole earth - all the peoples, all the languages, all the far-flung places. The rich diversity of the nations is not an accident of history; it flows from the plan of a God whose heart is for the whole world.

We can so easily shrink God down to our own group, our own kind, our own culture. But Genesis will not let us. It shows God as the Maker and Lord of every people on earth. The languages that sound strange to us, the cultures unlike our own - all are known and loved by God.

This world-embracing heart of God comes to its climax in the gospel. God promised Abraham that through him "all peoples on earth will be blessed" (Gen 12:3), and in Christ that promise is fulfilled, as people "from every nation, tribe, people and language" are gathered before God's throne (Rev 7:9). The God of the nations wants people from every one of them. His heart is bigger than our borders - and so should ours be.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you see God as the God of all nations, not just your own?
- How can you share God's heart for peoples different from you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord of all nations, thank You that Your heart embraces every people, language, and land. Enlarge my heart beyond my own borders, and help me long, as You do, for people from every nation to know You.
